note: Optional blocks — add one only when the memo needs it; without them the memo comes out in the basic layout. Illustrative shape only (same made-up case as the example) — do not reuse the content.

when.head.to / head.basis / head.workings: The addressee, the documents relied on with the as-of date of the law, and the file name of the Excel workings that go with the memo.
when.workings_check: Give it whenever head.workings is set. Finish the Excel and check it before writing the memo: made with export_workbook (korean-tax-calc-mcp) → method "export_workbook"; built yourself → run verify_workbook on the saved file and copy its counts (checked, mismatched, unchecked) with a one- or two-sentence unchecked_note and the file name of the copy with the check sheet; no check run → method "none". Amounts not checked also go under limitations. Printed as one fixed sentence in the closing paragraph. With unchecked above 0, e.g. {"method": "verify_workbook", "checked": 6, "mismatched": 0, "unchecked": 1, "unchecked_note": "The day count on the inputs sheet was typed in from the bank record and is not a calculator result."}, the same point is listed under limitations.
when.key_figures: The answer is a set of numbers, or two or three scenarios must be compared side by side. Printed right under the short answer.
when.analysis[].table: A short computation or comparison that belongs to one issue. Goes inside that analysis item as "table".
when.review: The question asks whether something already done was right. One bold verdict sentence plus one finding per problem.
when.action_list: Next steps as a table with owner and deadline. Use instead of next_steps; every item needs a deadline.
when.limitations: Anything you could not confirm, collected in one place. Required once any field or footnote says not verified.
when.authorities: Closing list of principal authorities. Off by default — the footnotes already carry the sources.
